claim.why_it_matters: A section heading demoted to plain text drops it from the document structure, so heading-based navigation and section slicing miss the clause boundary.
claim.note: Printed as a section heading (sibling of 3.9.3); the markdown renders it as a plain paragraph with no heading marker.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page XIII-23 (PDF p605) sets '3.9.4 General Rules' as a numbered clause heading after Table 1, laid out like the other numbered subclause headings. In the transcription (page-605.md line 23; specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 22892) it is a bare paragraph with no '#' marker. Its siblings in the same Report Group Description Entry clause, '### 3.9.1 Function' (line 22700) and '### 3.9.2 General Format' (line 22704), are marked headings, and the parallel clause at line 16303 is '## 3.9.4 General Rules'. The text is the same in both sources. Only the heading markup is missing, which loses the clause boundary for heading-based slicing. It is a structural defect, not a normative one. 3.9.3 Syntax Rules (line 22808) is also unmarked, but that heading is on another page and is not part of this claim.
